title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: logged-in user email on the Windows device onboarding page (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing's roadmap facts, client prerequisite and device-data read routes are supported. Licensing should name the published Endpoint DLP entitlement rather than remain wholly unknown; the role-review checklist also names a control missing from the table.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Risk assessment
claims.claim: Microsoft plans to show logged-in user email on the Purview device onboarding page for Windows devices.
claims.quote: This update introduces logged-in user details (user email) on the device onboarding page for Windows devices

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the Windows display as bringing it into line with the existing macOS experience.
claims.quote: bringing it in line with the experience for MacOS devices.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The roadmap says admins can see the currently signed-in user to confirm ownership and troubleshoot issues faster.
claims.quote: Admins can now see which user is currently signed in on a device, making It faster to confirm ownership and troubleshoot issues.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Learn explicitly identifies roadmap item 548669 and requires Anti-malware Client Version 4.18.26030 or newer.
claims.quote: Logged-in user details (user email) on the device onboarding page (Roadmap ID 548669) | Anti-malware Client Version 4.18.26030 or newer is required.

claims.claim: The feature prerequisite row links Windows update details for the Windows versions it lists.
claims.quote: Windows 10: See update details Windows 11 22H2: See update details Windows 11 23H2: See update details Windows 11 24H2: See update details

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Scope; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated the display's default state or rollout mechanics.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device onboarding logged-in user details enable disable default; "Purview" "logged-in user" "default". Read device-onboarding-overview and dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync; neither states the display's default or rollout mechanics.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The licensing model is unknown because no licence specific to the new display is published.
claims.quote:
| Feature | Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW and Microsoft Defender + Purview Suite FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection & Governance |
| --- | --- |
| Endpoint Data Loss Prevention (DLP) | Included |
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes with: 'Endpoint DLP is included in Microsoft 365 E5, among the eligible plans listed in the Microsoft Purview service description. Microsoft has not published a licence statement specific to this display.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/office365/servicedescriptions/microsoft-365-service-descriptions/microsoft-365-tenantlevel-services-licensing-guidance/microsoft-purview-service-description. In the cost rationale, replace 'licensing for it is not yet published' with 'a licence statement specific to this display is not yet published'. This is the standard's minor understatement where product-level licensing is published.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The onboarding overview points to Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans and service descriptions without naming a licence specifically for this display.
claims.quote:
For information on licensing, see
- Microsoft 365 Enterprise Plans
- Microsoft 365 Service Descriptions

claims.claim: A licence statement specific to logged-in user email on the onboarding page is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP device onboarding licensing user details billing meter; "548669" "user" "license". Read onboarding overview and Purview service description: product-level Endpoint DLP plans are given, but no display-specific entitlement.

claims.claim: No meter is documented specifically for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview Endpoint DLP device onboarding licensing user details billing meter. Read device-onboarding-overview, Microsoft Purview service description and purview-billing-models; no meter for this display is listed.

claims.claim: The Devices read route is Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Open the Microsoft Purview portal. Choose Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" reads existing Endpoint DLP device data.
claims.quote:
Sample query:
DeviceInfo
| where DlpInfo != ""
| project DlpInfo

claims.claim: The DeviceInfo query runs in Advanced hunting in the Microsoft Defender portal.
claims.quote:
Go to the Microsoft Defender portal
Navigate to Investigation & response > Hunting > Advanced hunting
Query the DeviceInfo table

claims.claim: The first control row gives read routes for device data rather than a switch controlling the new display.
claims.quote: In addition to viewing device attributes in the Microsoft Purview portal, you can access the same Endpoint DLP device data through the DeviceInfo table in Advanced hunting.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and controls[1].api; summary; Governance controls
claims.claim: No separate UI or API switch to turn logged-in user details on or off is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview logged-in user details device onboarding disable enable setting PowerShell user email default; "device onboarding" "user" "Set-DlpCompliancePolicy" email display. Read onboarding overview and troubleshooting page; no display-specific switch found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance controls
claims.claim: Device management supports Entra roles, not Purview roles.
claims.quote: Device management currently only supports Entra roles. Purview roles are not supported.

claims.claim: A custom account viewing device management settings needs one of Compliance admin, Compliance data admin, Global reader, Security admin or Global admin.
claims.quote:
If you want to use a custom account to view the device management settings, it must be in one of these roles:
- Compliance admin
- Compliance data admin
- Global reader
- Security admin
- Global admin

claims.claim: No new permission specific to the logged-in user detail is described.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device onboarding logged in user email DlpUpn export permissions roles; "Purview" "logged-in user" "email" export roles permission. Read onboarding overview permissions and troubleshooting page; no new display-specific permission found.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not separately specified which roles see the new email detail.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device onboarding logged in user email DlpUpn export permissions roles. Read device-onboarding-overview permissions and dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync; general device-management roles are listed, but no per-role visibility rule for the new field.

claims.claim: The Devices page shows device configuration and policy sync status.
claims.quote: To view these details, go to Device onboarding > Devices. From there, you can review each device's current configuration state and confirm whether policies have successfully synced.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Valid user indicates whether the currently logged-on user has a corresponding Entra ID account and is in scope of a DLP policy targeted at Devices.
claims.quote: Valid user | This indicates if the currently logged on user has a corresponding Entra ID account and is in scope of a DLP policy that's targeted at Devices.

claims.claim: DlpUpn in DeviceInfo's DlpInfo object is the user principal name associated with the device.
claims.quote: DlpUpn | string | User principal name (UPN) associated with the device.

claims.claim: Learn says the DlpInfo data corresponds to information on the DLP device onboarding page.
claims.quote: These values correspond to the device information available in the DLP device onboarding page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The documentation does not explicitly identify the new display detail as a field in exports or DeviceInfo.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device onboarding logged in user email DlpUpn export permissions roles. Read onboarding overview and troubleshooting page: exports and DlpUpn exist, but neither explicitly ties them to roadmap 548669's new display.

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly equate DlpUpn with the value shown by the new logged-in user detail.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device onboarding logged in user email DlpUpn export permissions roles. Read dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync and device-onboarding-overview; DlpUpn is a device-associated UPN, without an explicit mapping to the new email display.

claims.claim: Endpoint DLP and insider risk management require Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices to be onboarded to send monitoring data.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) and insider risk management require that Windows 10 and Windows 11 devices be onboarded into the service so that they can send monitoring data to the services.

claims.claim: Device details provides Defender engine and client version attributes for checking device versions.
claims.quote:
From the Device details section, record the values for these fields:
- OS
- Defender engine version
- Defender client version
- MDATP device ID
- Valid user

claims.claim: Not updated and Not available are documented policy sync status values.
claims.quote: If the status is Not updated or Not available, follow the remediation steps in the details pane and the steps in the workflow diagram.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the precise placement or presentation of the new user email.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview device onboarding logged-in user details 548669 enable disable default email export DeviceInfo licensing meter. Read device-onboarding-overview and dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync; prerequisite is listed but no new email UI layout is described.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The roadmap describes an admin-facing information display, not an automated action on users or devices or a change to the end-user experience.
claims.quote: This update introduces logged-in user details (user email) on the device onboarding page for Windows devices

claims.claim: The device-management page is available to administrative role holders rather than ordinary end users.
claims.quote:
If you want to use a custom account to view the device management settings, it must be in one of these roles:
- Compliance admin
- Compliance data admin
- Global reader
- Security admin
- Global admin

claims.claim: Every control the governance checklist asks readers to review has a corresponding controls-table row.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'List which Entra role holders can view device management settings'. Table rows cover device-data read routes and the absent display switch, not Entra role membership.
claims.fix: Remove the checklist bullet 'List which Entra role holders can view device management settings, and confirm each still needs to see device records.' It names a control without a corresponding row; do not add a new row in this correction.
